newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore exchange rate determined by demand - Hu.
newsitem.headline: Singapore exchange rate determined by demand - Hu.

text.p: Singapore's exchange rate is determined by market demand and its recent strength against some regional currencies has not affected the country's export competitiveness, said Finance Minister Richard Hu on Wednesday.
Hu, speaking in parliament, gave a breakdown of how the Singapore dollar had fared during the recent weakness in regional currencies.
He said the Singapore dollar had appreciated by only 3.5 percent against the Philippine peso and had in fact depreciated by 0.4 percent against the Malaysian ringgit.
Against the Thai baht, the Singapore dollar had appreciated "substantially" by 13.5 percent, and against the rupiah by 6.9 percent, he said.

"But the appreciation against these two countries should not pose a significant threat to our competitiveness because the composition of our exports differs considerably from the export packages of Thailand and Indonesia."
Hu said Singapore's competitiveness should be viewed on a longer-term perspective.

"Our exchange rate policy should not be guided by short-term expediency considerations. We always focus on managing the exchange rate of the Singapore dollar on a trade-weighted basis with a medium-term perspective."
He said this approach had shielded the Singapore dollar from "the sharp currency misalignments" experienced by countries which pegged their currencies to the U.S. dollar.
"We also manage our exchange rate flexibly so as to cater for market fluctuations. The Singapore dollar exchange rate is determined by market demand for our currency," Hu added.
